reviews.title: Extremely difficult to cancel
reviews.text:
Use extreme caution before starting a free trial with Creed.

I attempted to cancel before being charged, but there was no functional way for me to do so through the app. The subscription management link directed me to Stripe, which required access to an email address I have never had access to.

I contacted Creed Support four separate times and repeatedly explained that I could not access the subscription. Instead of canceling it, they continued sending generic responses and directing me back to the same Stripe portal I had already told them I could not access.

Creed was eventually able to locate the subscription using my user ID, proving that they could identify the account. However, they still did not immediately cancel it or correct the inaccessible email address.

A customer should not have to send repeated emails, threaten a payment dispute, and publicly complain just to stop a free trial from becoming a paid subscription. This has been one of the most frustrating customer service experiences I have had. I cannot recommend giving this company your payment information until they provide a clear, accessible cancellation process and responsive customer support.

reviews.title: Pay walls are putting up boundaries between people and Christ.
reviews.text: I really love the basis of the app, it felt great to have a device that would connect me to God and help me understand my deeper questions about faith, I even recommended it to newcomer to Christianity, only to realize that it is an inflexible system that requires payment. If it were simply limited per day for the amount of things you can say as an unsubscribed individual, that would be okay, but forcing users to pay to seek religious guidance isn’t Christ-like. I want to be able to enrich my connection to The Lord, but these pay walls are crippling my ability to do so. I think there should be a free version with limited chat amounts rather than a full bat against users having the app for free.

reviews.title: Mark 11:17
reviews.text:
I believe in supporting good work, but faith should never feel like it’s being sold. When core spiritual content is placed behind a paywall, it creates a barrier between people and God that shouldn’t exist. Jesus spoke strongly against turning worship into a marketplace, and that warning still matters today.

Charging for optional tools or extra features makes sense, but access to Scripture, prayer, and spiritual growth should be freely available to everyone. I hope this app reconsiders how it approaches payments so it reflects the heart of the Gospel open, accessible, and centered on God, not profit.

reviews.title: Need a companion, not a school marm
reviews.text: The app is a great idea. I am sure the creators will dial it in over time. I may come back to it. I'm leaving my account today. I struggle with three big things. First, the voice goes on and on. He lectures way too much. I need a companion for the road not someone telling me everything I do wrong. There is a lack of empathy in what the voice is saying. second, I think choosing a sheep for the mascot is hysterical. Sheep, as we've often been told, are stupid and that's why WE are called sheep. Wouldn't it be better to have an owl or lion or an animal that is affiliated with wisdom? Thirdly, he interrupts way too quickly. He gets in the way of my thought process and trying to ask a question.
